newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK airlines cancel more flights after groundings.
newsitem.headline: HK airlines cancel more flights after groundings.

text.p: Passengers flying with Hong Kong's two airlines faced delays and cancellations for the second day on Sunday after the two carriers grounded their Airbus A330-300 fleets over concerns about engine safety.

"We've got 15 flights cancelled today and doing our best where possible to get all our passengers onto other flights," a Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd spokeswoman told Reuters, adding that some schedules had been changed.
"Some flights may be doubling up where we've got capacity -- a London flight may stop en route or something like that."

Cathay Pacific suspended 11 Airbus A330-300 aircraft on Saturday and sister carrier Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd (Dragonair) suspended four after a series of single-engine landings involving Rolls-Royce Trent 700 engines.

Sunday's cancellations affected Cathay Pacific's flights to London, Zurich, Tokyo, Osaka, Bangkok, Singapore and Melbourne as well as round-trips on the Taipei, Nagoya, Saigon and Denpasar routes, the airline said in a statement.
Dragonair cancelled flights to Sendai, Hiroshima, Haikou, Chongqing and two to Kaohsiung, a spokesman said.
On Saturday, the two airlines cancelled 25 flights and rescheduled several others, stranding or inconveniencing thousands of passengers at Hong Kong's Kai Tak airport.

The groundings on Saturday followed an emergency landing by a Dragonair A330 at Subic Bay in the Philippines on Friday after the plane developed trouble in one of its two Trent 700 engines en route from Hong Kong to Kota Kinabalu in Malaysia.
It was the fifth time since November a Cathay Pacific or Dragonair Airbus A330-300 had made a single-engine landing.

"We're hoping for a solution quickly," the Cathay Pacific spokeswoman said. "If we're going to be without these 11 aircraft for a while we will probably look at leasing aircraft. At the moment we haven't got any additional aircraft, we're just coping with our own."

Dragonair was relying on the other seven planes in its fleet -- Airbus A320s fitted with IAE V2500 engines -- as well as other carriers, he said, adding that an extra flight to Kaohsiung on Sunday was operated by China Airlines.
The Airbus A330-300s will be grounded for "a few weeks", the Dragonair spokesman said. But the Cathay Pacific spokeswoman said reports of a three-week suspension were "speculation".
The two carriers said on Saturday they took the precaution of grounding the A330-300s until Rolls-Royce could provide assurances about the reliability of the engine in question.
On Friday, Rolls-Royce said gearbox bearings were to blame for the problems with the Trent 700s, which were introduced in March 1995.
"We are replacing the affected parts," a spokeswoman said.

Cathay Pacific, Dragonair and Indonesian flag carrier Garuda Indonesia are the only airlines now using the Trent 700, although Rolls-Royce said it has orders for at least 60 of the engines from carriers such as TWA, Gulf Air and Emirates.
Garuda said it intends to continue flying its six A330-300s with Trent 700s.
Swire Pacific Ltd and Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd together hold about 26 percent of Dragonair, whose major shareholder is China National Aviation Corp.
